instruction: more_itertools.exactly_n(iterable, n, predicate=bool) mishandles negative n: exactly_n([True], -10) raises ValueError instead of answering. No iterable has a negative number of true items, so a negative n must return False (exactly_n([], -1), exactly_n([], -10) and exactly_n([True], -10) are all False). The rest stays as it is: exactly_n([True], 0) is False, exactly_n([False, False], 0) is True, it stops reading once more than n items satisfy the predicate (so exactly_n(itertools.repeat(True), 100) returns False), and exactly_n(itertools.repeat(False, 100), 100, predicate=operator.not_) is True.
